title: Service retrospect announce crib memo
content:
Notes / scratchpad for an internal announcement + Q&A we can adapt for all-hands and CS/Sales. Rough: very conversational, quick bullets, fill gaps before we make anything public.

Goal: produce a short internal announcement (one-paragraph) + longer Q&A crib for folks who will be asked details. Keep customer-facing language non-technical and accountable. Flag open items clearly.

High-level summary (one-paragraph draft):
- Yesterday (2026-03-10) at ~14:23 UTC a memory leak in the serving runtime for model-family 'redwood-7b-opt' caused elevated latency and a small percentage of request failures for a subset of Dedicated and Hosted instances. We mitigated the issue by rolling back the most recent kernel change, restarting affected pools, and applying a temporary memory cap policy. The incident lasted ~47 minutes for most tenants; we continued monitoring and validated normal traffic patterns by 15:20 UTC. No customer data was exposed.

Timeline (quick):
- 14:20 UTC: alerts trigger (increased OOM/latency metrics on gpm-rt-02 pool)
- 14:23 UTC: page to oncall SRE (rowan)
- 14:27 UTC: initial triage — error traces show KV cache allocations steadily growing beyond expected bounds after new kernel selector change (PR #4521)
- 14:35 UTC: roll forward attempts cause lingering instability -> decide rollback
- 14:39 UTC: rollback PR #4521 initiated, affected nodes drained and restarted with safe kernel profile
- 15:05 UTC: traffic patterns normalizing; continued verification
- 15:20 UTC: declared mitigated; post-incident monitoring window opened

Customer impact summary (for CS):
- Affected: small subset (~3% peak) of requests to redwood-7b-opt across Hosted API and a few Dedicated pools in us-west1.
- Symptoms: occasional 5xx errors and higher tail latency for short period; majority of requests served normally.
- Data exposure: none identified.
- Billing/credits: TBD — recommend offering a small goodwill credit for affected customers if they open a support case; CS to coordinate with finance.

Draft customer note (short):
Hi <Customer>,
We experienced a short service disruption earlier today affecting a small percentage of requests for some model variants. Our team identified the cause as a memory regression in a runtime optimization and applied a fix; services were restored within one hour. We’re continuing a full review and will share final findings and any remediation steps in our postmortem. We apologize for the interruption and are available if you have any concerns.

Internal Q&A crib (for Slack / All-hands):
Q: How widespread was this?
A: Peak effect hit ~3% of requests to redwood-7b-opt; mostly seen in us-west1 pools. Not a global outage, but measurable for some tenants.

Q: Root cause?
A: Regression in kernel selector that caused KV cache allocations to bypass the expected eviction path under long prompt sequences. The change was merged as PR #4521 last week. Full RCA in Confluence.

Q: Why did rollback take ~16 minutes?
A: Draining stateful serving nodes with large KV caches requires careful restarts to avoid extra user-facing errors; we opted for a controlled drain+restart rather than forceful kill. That extended the mitigation window but reduced the risk of cascading failures.

Q: Any customer data risk?
A: No. There was no access to persistence or logs beyond normal operational telemetry. Security reviewed the traces during the incident.

Q: What are next steps / remediation?
A: Short term: revert kernel selector by default, apply safe memory cap. Medium term: add unit tests for KV cache eviction edgecases, expand canary coverage to include long-prompt workloads, and add a circuit-breaker telemetry alert for anomalous per-request allocation growth. Owner: eng-serving-runtime (PRs scheduled).

Q: Will this slow down future improvements?
A: We will be more conservative with kernel selector rollouts until additional tests and canaries are in place; this is temporary. The long-term optimization work will continue with safer deployment controls.

Talking points for CEO / Exec drop-in (one-liners):
- We had a brief degradation affecting a small portion of traffic; mitigated within an hour with no data exposure.
- We are prioritizing follow-ups to prevent recurrence and will share a public postmortem once technical fixes are complete.

Action items (who/what):
- eng-serving-runtime: formal RCA draft + PRs for tests and selector fallback (owner: Rowan Li)
- eng-sre: add allocation-growth alert and run a simulated long-prompt canary (owner: Lila Shah)
- CS/Sales: prepare proactive outreach list for customers who reported errors; if they request credit coordinate with finance (owner: Aisha Khan)
- Product/Trust: prepare public postmortem and customer FAQ (owner: Evelyn Park)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide exact credit policy threshold — propose manual approval for credits > $1k
- Confirm whether any Dedicated customers hit SLA thresholds; ask billing team for quick query
- Validate canary runs in eu-west region (we only ran us-west canary last month)
- Cross-check kernel selector change logs for similar changes in other model-families

Draft all-hands script (30s):
- Quick note: yesterday we saw a short incident where a runtime optimization caused increased errors for a small subset of traffic. We reverted the change and restored normal service; there was no data exposure. Full RCA and remediation plan are in progress — we’ll publish a postmortem next week. Thanks to the oncall and runtime teams for the quick mitigation.

Tone reminders:
- Be concise, accountable, avoid technical jargon in customer-facing comms.
- Internally it's fine to be technical and name PRs and owners.
- When in doubt, defer to SRE/Trust for any phrasing that touches security or data handling.

Versions / local draft notes:
- v0.1 (this): crib + timeline + Q&A
- v0.2: incorporate Rowan's RCA notes and Evelyn's customer blurb
- v1.0: final internal announcement + customer note + public postmortem link

References: JIRA-INC-1728, PR #4521, confluence:incident/INC-1728-postmortem, slack:#inc-1728-thread

Scratch/brain dump:
- Might pitch a short blog post on how canaries caught (or missed) this regression and what we improved — good PR for developer trust.
- Consider adding a short 'how we tested' section to public postmortem so customers understand we validate production scale.

End of scratchpad.

(leave as is until Rowan/Aisha/Evelyn add their notes then move to shared_drives/company/messaging for finalization)
